doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The good old days and the 1955 Birdland All-Stars tour
summary: Gibbs says every year had highlights, recalls hearing Duke Ellington's introduction, and lists the Birdland All-Stars tour lineup.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well you answered my next question. I was going to ask you —
I got this crystal ball. I knew that —
The question was does Terry Gibbs think that there were good old days in his life? And it seems like almost without exception they were all —

All great. Really okay. There was really something every year that was really great and stuck out you know. And let me tell you, let’s face it, when you get a chance growing up listening to Benny Goodman and Duke Ellington and get to know these people, get to know these people. You know like I’ve been on the scene with the Dream Band one time when Duke Ellington introduced the band, and I didn’t want to follow it, because that introduction was so great that whatever I played, it would be ridiculous. I mean Duke Ellington was so elegant with his speaking, God, I said I was going to say, “Listen, I’m the greatest, he just said that.” You know. So the point is I was blessed to have known these people, know them personally. You know I’ll tell you Dizzy Gillespie and I hung out — I did a tour that I did well I’m going to tell you, one show, I probably wrote about that. Yeah the Birdland All-Stars of 1955 or whatever, 7. Billy Eckstine, the headliner with Bobby Tucker played piano, and Sarah Vaughan and Roy Haynes and Jimmy Jones on piano, the Count Basie Band when he had Joe Williams, Frank Foster, Frank Wess, Hank Jones, all the — Sonny Payne, Lester Young, Zoot Sims, Chet Baker’s group, Jeri
Southern, Phineas Newborn, Bud Powell. For two months, can you do better than that if you want to play with people? Who’s left?
You’ve already been to heaven, Terry.
I was, I still am. I’m still talking to you. I’m not sure what I’m saying but I’m talking to you.
